theses.title: Memory is the new GPU: AI inference shifts the bottleneck from logic to HBM/DRAM/NAND bits
chain: AI capex has over-provisioned GPU compute but each inference token consumes memory bandwidth and capacity, not just FLOPs
HBM attention jumped +72% across filers while its basket is up only +2% — companies are talking about it, the market has not re-rated the owners (A)
NAND scarcity language exploded +884% and DRAM +392% off a near-zero base, and the voices are DEMAND-side buyers (AAPL, LI, MU) flagging they cannot get bits (B)
Memory fabs are capex- and yield-constrained; HBM steals wafer capacity from commodity DRAM/NAND, so a demand shock tightens the WHOLE memory complex, not one node
Owners of the constrained bit supply (MU, SNDK, WDC) see ASPs and margins inflect while the tape still prices them as late-cycle commodity cyclicals
theses.bottleneck: HBM/DRAM/NAND bit supply and memory-fab wafer capacity
theses.whyNow: NAND/DRAM scarcity language is up ~400-900% off zero (B) and HBM attention +72% with basket +2% (A) — the attention/price gap is widest here of any concept
theses.pricedIn: Almost nothing: HBM basket +2%, NAND/DRAM scarcity baskets ~-1% (A,B). Smart money disagrees with the tape — SA LP holds 56% in SNDK+MU (D)
theses.killCriteria: DRAM/NAND spot contract prices roll over 2 quarters in a row, HBM qualification orders from hyperscalers get pushed, or memory makers guide capex UP into a demand air-pocket (classic top). Any of these within 6 months kills it.

theses.title: Power and the electrical interconnect, not silicon, is the hard physical ceiling on the AI buildout
chain: A data center is useless without megawatts delivered to the rack; the US grid, transformers, and switchgear have decade-long lead times
grid scarcity language +78% and data-center scarcity +25% (B), yet the grid basket is -13% and data-center basket -5% (A) — the constraint is loud but unpriced
The named scarcity voices are the builders themselves (CORZ, IREN, GDS, AAON on data center; CLF, FE, NRG on grid) (B) — supply-side capitulation, not hype
Electrical-equipment and power-gen owners (GEV, ETN, VRT, CEG, VST) sell into multi-year backlogs with pricing power as utilities and hyperscalers bid for scarce capacity
Earnings must rise because backlog coverage and book-to-bill expand while the component (transformers, cooling, firm power) stays sold out
theses.bottleneck: Grid interconnect capacity, high-voltage electrical gear, and firm 24/7 power
theses.whyNow: Grid scarcity +78% and data-center scarcity +25% are among the fastest-rising shortage signals (B) while the baskets are deeply negative (A)
theses.pricedIn: Lightly: grid basket -13%, data-center -5% (A). Note 'transformer' basket is -12% (A) — that sub-theme already ran and corrected, so I lean to grid/electrical breadth not transformers specifically
theses.killCriteria: Hyperscaler capex guides flat/down for 2026, data-center interconnect queues start clearing, or GEV/ETN/VRT book-to-bill drops below 1.0 within 6 months.

theses.title: HBM and advanced packaging are etch-and-deposition intensive — the pick-and-shovel layer under the memory shock
chain: HBM stacks and advanced packaging (hybrid bonding, TSV) require far more etch/deposition steps per wafer than planar logic
etch attention +51% and deposition +3% with baskets roughly flat (-2%/-1%) (A) — rising mention, no price
If Thesis 1 (memory shortage) is right, memory-makers must add capacity, and capacity = WFE orders to the etch/deposition/inspection leaders
Owners (LRCX, AMAT, KLAC, ONTO, ACMR) capture the capex regardless of which memory maker wins the HBM share war — a lower-variance way to own the memory bottleneck
Their earnings rise as memory WFE re-accelerates off a trough while the market still models flat 2026 WFE
theses.bottleneck: Advanced etch/deposition/inspection tool capacity for HBM and packaging
theses.whyNow: etch attention +51% (A) directly precedes the memory-capacity response implied by the +884% NAND scarcity signal (B)
theses.pricedIn: Modestly: etch/deposition baskets ~flat (A). GPU basket +4% shows the logic-WFE leg is more discovered than the memory-WFE leg
theses.killCriteria: Memory makers cut or delay capex, LRCX/AMAT memory-segment revenue mix shrinks for 2 quarters, or China WFE restrictions deepen enough to offset HBM demand — within 6 months.

theses.title: Foundry and EUV are the un-substitutable chokepoint — own the toll-booth
chain: Every leading-edge AI chip and HBM base-die routes through TSMC; CoWoS advanced-packaging capacity is the single tightest line in the AI supply chain
EUV lithography has one supplier (ASML); there is no second source at the node
Inference attention +26% and data-center breadth across 284 cos (A) means volume, not just price, flows through the one foundry and the one litho vendor
Earnings must rise because TSMC prices CoWoS/leading-edge up into scarcity and ASML's backlog is multi-year and order-covered
SA LP holds TSM at 6% (D) — the smart-money anchor agrees this is the durable toll
theses.bottleneck: Leading-edge foundry + CoWoS packaging (TSM) and EUV scanners (ASML)
theses.whyNow: This is the lower-beta anchor to the memory/power theses; inference +26% broadens the demand base (A)
theses.pricedIn: Partially — these are consensus AI winners, so sized smaller than the unpriced memory/grid legs. Edge is durability, not surprise.
theses.killCriteria: TSMC CoWoS capacity additions outrun demand (utilization dips), ASML bookings miss for 2 quarters, or a credible leading-edge second source emerges within 6 months.

theses.title: Copper is the embedded commodity in every megawatt of AI power
chain: Electrification of data centers (Thesis 2) is copper-intensive: busbars, transformers, cabling, cooling
copper attention +13% with basket only -4% (A) — rising mention, price still soft
Mine supply is inelastic (decade-long permitting/ramp) while AI-power demand is a step-change on top of EV/grid baseline
Owners of low-cost copper reserves (FCX, SCCO) see realized prices rise against a fixed cost base, expanding margins
This is the second-derivative of the power thesis and the least-crowded expression of it
theses.bottleneck: Mined copper supply vs. electrification demand
theses.whyNow: copper attention +13% while grid/data-center scarcity surges (A,B) — demand signal building, price not yet there
theses.pricedIn: Barely: copper basket -4% (A). Lowest-confidence leg because it's macro/China-sensitive, so sized small.
theses.killCriteria: China property/demand weakens further, copper inventories build, or a global-growth scare drops the price under cost-curve support within 6 months.

picks.rationale: Broadest memory-shortage leverage (HBM+DRAM+NAND); HBM attention +72%/basket +2% (A), DRAM scarcity +392% (B); SA LP top holding at 28% (D)
Pure NAND play into a +884% NAND scarcity signal off zero (B); SA LP's co-top holding at 28% (D) — strongest smart-money/tape divergence
Un-substitutable leading-edge + CoWoS toll-booth; inference +26% broadens volume (A); SA LP 6% (D); durable anchor
Etch leader; etch attention +51% basket -2% (A); captures memory capex regardless of who wins HBM share
Grid equipment into grid scarcity +78% basket -13% (A,B); multi-year backlog with pricing power
NAND/HDD capacity tightening (B); cheapest expression of the bit-shortage; mean-reversion torque if DRAM/NAND inflect
Deposition breadth; memory-WFE re-acceleration under-modeled vs. logic (GPU basket +4% already found, A)
EUV monopoly, order-covered multi-year backlog; lower-variance toll on the entire leading-edge buildout
Electrical gear into data-center scarcity +25% (B); book-to-bill driven by sold-out switchgear/power management
Power + thermal management for racks; direct beneficiary of data-center scarcity (B), server scarcity +7% (B)
Process control/inspection scales with advanced-packaging complexity; captures capex across all memory/foundry players
Nuclear baseload is the scarce firm power hyperscalers are signing PPAs for; grid scarcity +78% (B)
Largest-cap copper leverage to electrification; copper attention +13% basket -4% (A) — unpriced second-derivative of power
Merchant generation re-rates as AI load tightens regional power; complements CEG with cheaper beta
Leveraged to HBM/advanced-packaging metrology; small-cap torque on the packaging-intensity story (deposition +3%, A)
Wafer-clean steps multiply with HBM stacking; small-cap WFE leverage if memory capex re-accelerates
Low-cost, long-reserve copper; margin expansion on realized-price lift against fixed cost base

avoid.why: GPU is the DISCOVERED leg — GPU basket +4% (A) vs. flat/negative memory, grid and etch baskets. The un-priced edge is downstream of the GPU, not in it; capex concentration risk if hyperscaler spend plateaus.
AI agents basket +16% (A) — already priced; buying the narrative at the point of maximum attention, not an unpriced bottleneck.
AI-agents/application layer already ran (basket +16%, A); no physical bottleneck owned, valuation discounts the theme.
Optical transceiver basket +11% (A) — the only basket already clearly up; the optical leg of the buildout is priced, poor risk/reward vs. memory/power.
Same optical-transceiver crowding (basket +11%, A); chasing a theme that has already re-rated.
CPU basket already +7% (A), among the few positive baskets; licensing model doesn't own the physical memory/power/wafer bottleneck where the unpriced edge sits.
